title: On spatial decoherence in many-body systems
abstract: We study the dynamics of a many-body quantum system strongly interacting with a bosonic reservoir. The coupling is given by a potential operator for the system and it is linear in the field. We show that in the limit of infinite coupling strength the system undergoes instantaneous spatial decoherence. To resolve the decoherence process in time we consider large coupling strengths $λ$ and short times scaling as $t\propto λ^{-α}$, with $α\ge0$, in the limit $λ\rightarrow\infty$. On short time scales $α>1$ the dynamics is trivial while on longer ones $0\leα<1$ the decoherence is instantaneous. We show that the decoherence process is resolved exactly for $α=1$, defining the fine-grained time scale $τ=λt$. We construct an approximate effective evolution map of the many-body system with controlled error estimates. Generically, the effective dynamics is markovian, but not given by a dynamical semigroup. As a physical application we give a rigorous description of the phenomenon of localization of macroscopic quantum objects in position space.
summary: This paper rigorously studies spatial decoherence in many-body systems interacting with a bosonic environment. It derives an effective evolution map by analyzing the system dynamics in specific limits of coupling strength and time scaling. The key finding is the identification of a fine-grained time scale $\tau = \lambda t$ that resolves the decoherence process, providing a theoretical description of macroscopic quantum localization.
main_problem: The paper investigates the dynamics of a many-body quantum system coupled strongly to a bosonic reservoir, focusing specifically on the mechanism and timescale of spatial decoherence.
main_result: The decoherence process is shown to be exactly resolved at a fine-grained time scale $\tau = \lambda t$, leading to an effective evolution map that is generally Markovian but not described by a standard dynamical semigroup.
method: The analysis uses time evolution calculations involving the full Hamiltonian, employing Dyson series expansions and introducing a projection operator $P$ to analyze the system's evolution in different limits of coupling strength ($\lambda$) and time ($t$).
model_or_system: The system consists of an $N$-body quantum system in $d$ dimensions, coupled via a linear potential operator $G$ to a bosonic quantum field reservoir. The dynamics are governed by a total Hamiltonian $H = H_S + H_R + \lambda G \otimes \phi(g)$.
key_observables: The expectation value of system observables $\langle A \rangle_t$, the density matrix evolution $\rho_t$, and the degree of off-diagonal coherence.
important_parameters: The coupling strength $\lambda$, the time $t$, and the crucial scaling parameter $\alpha$ defining the time dependence $t \propto \lambda^{-\alpha}$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on considering the limit of infinite coupling strength ($\lambda \to \infty$) and assumes the reservoir state $\omega_R$ is regular (e.g., Gaussian).
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the time evolution under different scaling limits of $\lambda$ and $t$, establishing the Zeno limit ($\alpha=0$), the static limit ($\alpha>1$), and deriving the exact effective dynamics for the critical scaling $\alpha=1$.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, quantitative description of how environmental coupling drives quantum systems toward classical localization, which is central to understanding quantum-to-classical transitions in open quantum systems.
